Marta V: Quick follow-up from the geo-gating RFC — proposing a lightweight edge shim that enforces tenant region-allowlists and emits a deterministic soft-fallback
Sam K: Can you sketch the runtime boundaries? i.e. what lives at the edge vs control plane?
Marta V: Sure. High level:
  - Edge (Envoy): per-request enforcement using header `X-Region-Preference` + local cache of tenant policy. Fast reject/route-to-fallback.
  - Control plane: distribution of tenant allowlists, versions, and policy TTLs.
  - Fallback service: a lightweight, global proxy that can serve non-resident requests with legal metadata.
Raj P: My worry: relying on edge cache means policy staleness. What's our story for correctness vs latency?
Marta V: tradeoffs:
  - Strong correctness: force consult to control plane -> high tail latency (bad for sync calls).
  - Best-effort low-latency: edge cache with TTL + versioned policy header. We detect mismatches and async reconcile.
  - Hybrid (recommended): short TTL (30s), versioned sig + a signed header `X-Policy-Version`. If edge sees an unknown version, it falls back to consult (but with a local circuit-breaker).
Kevin L: How do we avoid incentivizing clients to set bogus `X-Region-Preference` to bypass policy?
Marta V: Edge must overwrite any incoming client hint with canonical decision header. clients can propose, but enforcement uses tenant binding.
Elaine (Legal): We need audit trails (who/when policy changed) + clear error classes for residency violations. Also retention for compliance.
Sam K: Implementation sketch (Envoy route config snippet):
```
    - match:
        prefix: "/v1/generate"
      route:
        cluster: regional-gatekeeper
      request_headers_to_add:
        - header:
            key: "x-policy-version"
            value: "%DYNAMIC_POLICY_VERSION%"
    ```
Marta V: Fallback behavior options: 1) reject (hard deny), 2) proxy to fallback service with masked PII + legal-metadata, 3) enqueue for async handling. Recommend (2) for PLG friendliness, but (1) for strict enterprise contracts.
Raj P: For (2) what's the security model? fallback service must live in a hardened tenant-scoped VPC and support per-tenant transforms.
Marta V: yes. We'll require mTLS + HSM-backed keys for header signing.
Kevin L: Ops questions: who deploys tenant policy updates? CR if manual, otherwise expose API for self-serve (with audit hooks). We should also rate-limit control-plane pulls during surge.
Marta V: Actionables:
  - (Sam) prototype Envoy filter + local policy cache (spike, 2w)
  - (Raj) threat model + fallback service security design (1w)
  - (Kevin) control-plane policy distribution API + burst protections (2w)
  - (Elaine) required audit fields + retention policy (sync now)
infra-bot: Scheduled deploy window for spike cluster: 2024-10-03T02:00Z (eta 3h) :rocket:
Sam K: One more Q — metrics: need per-tenant gate rate, fallback rate, policy-stale rate. Also a signal for edge-circuit trips.
Marta V: Agreed. We'll add a policy-monitoring dashboard and alerts for >0.1% stale-denies.
Elaine (Legal): Also escalate path for customers who need immediate policy exemptions.
Sam K: OK I'll start the spike branch today and post findings in this thread.
Marta V: Thanks — keeping this lightweight lets us iterate quickly while preserving legal guarantees. :white_check_mark:
